column3: “Seah” is rendered “measure,” and NASB supplies “shall be sold.”
NASB turns “Behold, the LORD is making windows” into a condition (“if the LORD should make windows”).
“Fall to the camp” is rendered “go over to the camp,” and “let us live” as “spare us.”
“Punishment will find us” is rendered “punishment will overtake us.”
NASB supplies “some men,” and “in any case” and “already perished.” The repeated Hebrew clause is probably a copying duplication.
“Two chariots, horses” is rendered “two chariots with horses,” and “camp” as “army.”
NASB again turns the statement into a condition (“if the LORD should make windows”).
